title: Adjustable Rate Rider — Summit Note Rate Resets
content:
**Rider terms.** The note rate of an adjustable plan of the Cedarline Summit Proprietary Reverse Mortgage resets every rate adjustment interval of its plan to the plan's index plus the loan's margin, never more than the plan's lifetime cap above the loan's initial note rate and never below the margin. A fixed plan's rate never changes. A Summit rate adjustment is recorded only while the loan status is active, draw period expired or due and payable.

## Definition of the new note rate

On each adjustment date the new note rate is the index value plus the margin, except that:

- where that sum is more than the initial note rate plus the lifetime cap, the new rate is the initial note rate plus the lifetime cap; and
- where that sum is below the margin, the new rate is the margin.

The initial note rate and the margin are those of the loan as fixed at closing; the cap is counted in percentage points over the initial note rate. The new rate takes effect on its adjustment date.

## Status at the adjustment date

| Loan status on the loan record | Rate adjustment recorded |
|---|---|
| Active | yes |
| Draw period expired | yes |
| Due and payable | yes |
| In its rescission period, rescinded, paid in full, liquidated | no |

## Worked resets (hypothetical figures, a cap of 10.00 percentage points)

Hypothetical loan: initial note rate 6.250%, margin 2.750%, so the highest possible note rate is 16.250% and the lowest is 2.750%.

| Hypothetical index value | Index plus margin | New note rate | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4.180% | 6.930% | 6.930% | between the margin and the cap |
| 14.020% | 16.770% | 16.250% | above the initial rate plus the cap |
| 13.500% | 16.250% | 16.250% | exactly at the cap, which is allowed |
| negative 0.040% | 2.710% | 2.750% | below the margin |

## Fixed plans

On a fixed plan no rate adjustment arises: the note rate set at closing stays for the life of the loan.
